Definition: from γοάω (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter:--seducer.
BiblicalUsage: góēs is a plain word for seducer. In 2 Timothy 3:13, the text says "But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse."
TheologicalSignificance: Out of góēs I do not force more than it gives: seducer.
